Nowadays it would be differential. Two times two current mirrors are added, i.e. with transistors M11/M12 and M13/M14. Without these transistors the maximum output current would be limited to BI . P In order to increase this maximum current, biasing current I must be made larger for larger p input voltages. This biasing current is adapted to the input signal level. This is why it is in parallel with two more current mirrors through transistors M18 and M19. Let us follow the path to transistor M19. Transistors M19 forms a current mirror (with current factor A) with M20. This latter transistor take the difference in current I –I , which are proportional to the currents in the input stage. 1 2 The larger of these two currents wins. commentary_text: An adaptive biasing amplifier adapts its biasing to be able to provide larger output currents. The amplifier in this slide is a symmetrical amplifier, which is single ended. Nowadays it would be differential. Two times two current mirrors are added, i.e. with transistors M11/M12 and M13/M14. Without these transistors the maximum output current would be limited to BI . P In order to increase this maximum current, biasing current I must be made larger for larger p input voltages. This biasing current is adapted to the input signal level. This is why it is in parallel with two more current mirrors through transistors M18 and M19. Let us follow the path to transistor M19. Transistors M19 forms a current mirror (with current factor A) with M20. This latter transistor take the difference in current I –I , which are proportional to the currents in the input stage. 1 2 The larger of these two currents wins. If I is larger than I then AI current is added to I , 1 2 1 p increasing the total biasing current of the first stage, and also increasing the maximum output current. If, however, I is larger than I , then it is mirrored by M17/M18, also multiplied by A and 2 1 also added to I . p The adaptive current feedback is a kind of rectifier, as shown next.
